sanskrit: na yamo nāntakaḥ kruddho na mṛtyur bhīmavikramaḥ īśate nṛpate sarve yogasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: Neither Yama, nor the wrathful Ender, nor Death of terrible prowess hold sway, O king, over the yogin whose splendor is measureless.

sanskrit: ātmanāṃ ca sahasrāṇi bahūni bharatarṣabha yogaḥ kuryād balaṃ prāpya taiś ca sarvair mahīṃ caret
english: Having attained power, O bull of the Bhāratas, yoga can fashion many thousands of selves, and with all of these the yogin may roam the earth.

sanskrit: prāpnuyād viṣayāṃś caiva punaś cograṃ tapaś caret saṃkṣipec ca punaḥ pārtha sūryas tejoguṇān iva
english: He may take possession of objects of sense, and again practice fierce austerity, and again draw them back in, O Pārtha, as the sun draws back the rays of its splendor.

sanskrit: balasthasya hi yogasya bandhaneśasya pārthiva vimokṣaprabhaviṣṇutvam upapannam asaṃśayam
english: For the yoga that is established in power and is lord over its own bondage, O ruler of the earth, the capacity to bring about liberation is assured beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: balāni yoge proktāni mayaitāni viśāṃ pate nidarśanārthaṃ sūkṣmāṇi vakṣyāmi ca punas tava
english: These powers in yoga have been declared by me, O lord of peoples; and by way of illustration I shall now further expound to you its subtle aspects.

sanskrit: ātmanaś ca samādhāne dhāraṇāṃ prati cābhibho nidarśanāni sūkṣmāṇi śṛṇu me bharatarṣabha
english: Concerning the concentration of the self and concerning steady fixation, O sovereign lord, hear from me the subtle illustrations, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: apramatto yathā dhanvī lakṣyaṃ hanti samāhitaḥ yuktaḥ samyak tathā yogī mokṣaṃ prāpnoty asaṃśayam
english: As the unwavering archer, fully composed, strikes the mark, so the yogin, rightly disciplined, attains liberation beyond all doubt.

sanskrit: snehapūrṇe yathā pātre mana ādhāya niścalam puruṣo yatta ārohet sopānaṃ yuktamānasaḥ
english: As a man, with mind fixed motionless upon a vessel brimming with oil, would mount the stair, vigilant and disciplined in thought—

sanskrit: yuktvā tathāyam ātmānaṃ yogaḥ pārthiva niścalam karoty amalam ātmānaṃ bhāskaropamadarśanam
english: so yoga, having yoked the self in that motionless way, O ruler of the earth, renders the self stainless and radiant as the sun to behold.

sanskrit: yathā ca nāvaṃ kaunteya karṇadhāraḥ samāhitaḥ mahārṇavagatāṃ śīghraṃ nayet pārthiva pattanam
english: And as a composed helmsman, O son of Kuntī, would swiftly steer a ship adrift upon the great ocean to the harbor, O ruler of the earth—

sanskrit: tadvad ātmasamādhānaṃ yuktvā yogena tattvavit durgamaṃ sthānam āpnoti hitvā deham imaṃ nṛpa
english: so the knower of truth, having yoked the concentration of the self through yoga, attains that station hard to reach, abandoning this body, O king.

sanskrit: sārathiś ca yathā yuktvā sadaśvān susamāhitaḥ deśam iṣṭaṃ nayaty āśu dhanvinaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: And as a charioteer, well composed, having yoked his fine steeds, swiftly bears the bowman to the desired place, O bull among men—

sanskrit: tathaiva nṛpate yogī dhāraṇāsu samāhitaḥ prāpnoty āśu paraṃ sthānaṃ lakṣaṃ mukta ivāśugaḥ
english: so too, O king, the yogin, composed in his fixations, swiftly attains the supreme station, as a loosed arrow reaches its mark.

sanskrit: āveśyātmani cātmānaṃ yogī tiṣṭhati yo 'calaḥ pāpaṃ hanteva mīnānāṃ padam āpnoti so 'jaram
english: The yogin who, having entered the self into the Self, stands unmoving—as the slayer of fish destroys evil—attains the ageless abode.

sanskrit: nābhyāṃ kaṇṭhe ca śīrṣe ca hṛdi vakṣasi pārśvayoḥ darśane sparśane cāpi ghrāṇe cāmitavikrama
english: In the navel, in the throat, in the head, in the heart, in the breast, in the two sides, and likewise in sight, in touch, and in smell, O man of measureless valor—

sanskrit: sthāneṣv eteṣu yo yogī mahāvratasamāhitaḥ ātmanā sūkṣmam ātmānaṃ yuṅkte samyag viśāṃ pate
english: the yogin who, in these stations, composed in the great vow, rightly yokes by the self the subtle Self, O lord of peoples—

sanskrit: sa śīghram amalaprajñaḥ karma dagdhvā śubhāśubham uttamaṃ yogam āsthāya yadīcchati vimucyate
english: he, swiftly of stainless wisdom, having burned away action both good and ill, taking his stand on the highest yoga, is liberated, if he so wishes.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca āhārān kīdṛśān kṛtvā kāni jitvā ca bhārata yogī balam avāpnoti tad bhavān vaktum arhati
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Taking what kind of food, and conquering what things, O descendant of Bharata, does the yogin attain power? This you ought to tell me.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca kaṇānāṃ bhakṣaṇe yuktaḥ piṇyākasya ca bhakṣaṇe snehānāṃ varjane yukto yogī balam avāpnuyāt
english: Bhīṣma said: Devoted to eating broken grains and oil-cake, and devoted to abstaining from oily foods, the yogin would attain power.

sanskrit: bhuñjāno yāvakaṃ rūkṣaṃ dīrghakālam ariṃdama ekārāmo viśuddhātmā yogī balam avāpnuyāt
english: Eating coarse barley-gruel for a long time, O subduer of foes, delighting in solitude, his self wholly purified, the yogin would attain power.

sanskrit: pakṣān māsān ṛtūṃś citrān saṃcaraṃś ca guhās tathā apaḥ pītvā payomiśrā yogī balam avāpnuyāt
english: Passing through fortnights, months, and the varied seasons, and roaming through caves, drinking water mingled with milk, the yogin would attain power.

sanskrit: akhaṇḍam api vā māsaṃ satataṃ manujeśvara upoṣya samyak śuddhātmā yogī balam avāpnuyāt
english: Or, fasting unbrokenly for a whole month continuously, O lord of men, his self rightly purified, the yogin would attain power.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ jitvā tathā krodhaṃ śītoṣṇe varṣam eva ca bhayaṃ nidrāṃ tathā śvāsaṃ pauruṣaṃ viṣayāṃs tathā
english: Conquering desire and likewise anger, cold and heat, and the rains, fear, sleep, and breath, manly pride and the objects of sense—

sanskrit: aratiṃ durjayāṃ caiva ghorāṃ tṛṣṇāṃ ca pārthiva sparśān sarvāṃs tathā tandrīṃ durjayāṃ nṛpasattama
english: discontent hard to conquer, and dreadful craving, O ruler of the earth, all sensations of touch, and torpor hard to conquer, O best of kings—

sanskrit: dīpayanti mahātmānaḥ sūkṣmam ātmānam ātmanā vītarāgā mahāprājñā dhyānādhyayanasaṃpadā
english: the great-souled ones, free from passion, of vast wisdom, kindle the subtle Self by the self through the riches of meditation and study.

sanskrit: durgas tv eṣa mataḥ panthā brāhmaṇānāṃ vipaścitām na kaś cid vrajati hy asmin kṣemeṇa bharatarṣabha
english: But this is held to be a hard road, that of the learned brāhmaṇas; for none travels upon it in safety, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yathā kaś cid vanaṃ ghoraṃ bahusarpasarīsṛpam śvabhravat toyahīnaṃ ca durgamaṃ bahukaṇṭakam
english: As some young man might safely make his way through a dreadful forest, full of many snakes and creeping things, pitted with holes, devoid of water, hard to pass, thick with thorns—

sanskrit: abhaktam aṭavīprāyaṃ dāvadagdhamahīruham panthānaṃ taskarākīrṇaṃ kṣemeṇābhipated yuvā
english: a road untrodden, wilderness-like, its trees scorched by forest fire, infested with robbers—safely traversing it,

sanskrit: yogamārgaṃ tathāsādya yaḥ kaś cid bhajate dvijaḥ kṣemeṇoparamen mārgād bahudoṣo hi sa smṛtaḥ
english: so when any twice-born one, having reached the path of yoga, practices it, should he safely turn back from that road, he is held to be greatly at fault.

sanskrit: sustheyaṃ kṣuradhārāsu niśitāsu mahīpate dhāraṇāsu tu yogasya duḥstheyam akṛtātmabhiḥ
english: It is easier to stand firm upon the sharpened edges of razors, O lord of the earth, than to stand firm in the fixations of yoga for those whose selves are unperfected.

sanskrit: vipannā dhāraṇās tāta nayanti naśubhāṃ gatim netṛhīnā yathā nāvaḥ puruṣān arṇave nṛpa
english: Fixations gone awry, my son, lead one to an unhappy state, as ships without a pilot lead men astray upon the ocean, O king.

sanskrit: yas tu tiṣṭhati kaunteya dhāraṇāsu yathāvidhi maraṇaṃ janma duḥkhaṃ ca sukhaṃ ca sa vimuñcati
english: But he who stands firm, O son of Kuntī, in the fixations as prescribed, casts off death and birth, sorrow and joy alike.

sanskrit: nānāśāstreṣu niṣpannaṃ yogeṣv idam udāhṛtam paraṃ yogaṃ tu yat kṛtsnaṃ niścitaṃ tad dvijātiṣu
english: This, perfected in the various treatises, has been set forth among the yogas; but the supreme yoga in its entirety is determined among the twice-born.

sanskrit: paraṃ hi tad brahma mahan mahātman; brahmāṇam īśaṃ varadaṃ ca viṣṇum bhavaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca ṣaḍānanaṃ ca; ṣaḍ brahmaputrāṃś ca mahānubhāvān
english: For that is the supreme, the great Brahman, O great-souled one—Brahmā the lord, and Viṣṇu the boon-giver, and Bhava, and Dharma, and the six-faced one, and the six mighty sons of Brahmā—

sanskrit: tamaś ca kaṣṭaṃ sumahad rajaś ca; sattvaṃ ca śuddhaṃ prakṛtiṃ parāṃ ca siddhiṃ ca devīṃ varuṇasya patnīṃ; tejaś ca kṛtsnaṃ sumahac ca dhairyam
english: and grievous, vast darkness, and passion, and pure goodness, and the supreme primordial nature, and the goddess Siddhi, the wife of Varuṇa, and splendor entire, and great steadfastness—

sanskrit: tārādhipaṃ vai vimalaṃ satāraṃ; viśvāṃś ca devān uragān pitṝṃś ca śailāṃś ca kṛtsnān udadhīṃś ca ghorān; nadīś ca sarvāḥ savanān ghanāṃś ca
english: the stainless lord of stars with its constellations, and all the gods, the serpents and the ancestors, all the mountains and the dreadful oceans, all the rivers, the woodlands, and the clouds—

sanskrit: nāgān nagān yakṣagaṇān diśaś ca; gandharvasaṃghān puruṣān striyaś ca parasparaṃ prāpya mahān mahātmā; viśeta yogī nacirād vimuktaḥ
english: the serpents, the mountains, the hosts of yakṣas and the quarters of space, the throngs of gandharvas, men and women—reaching each in turn, the great and great-souled yogin would enter in, liberated ere long.

sanskrit: kathā ca yeyaṃ nṛpate prasaktā; deve mahāvīryamatau śubheyam yogān sa sarvān abhibhūya martyān; nārāyaṇātmā kurute mahātmā
english: And this auspicious discourse, O king, which has dwelt upon the god of mighty valor and wisdom—the great-souled one, his soul become Nārāyaṇa, surpasses all the yogas of mortals.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca samyak tvayāyaṃ nṛpate varṇitaḥ śiṣṭasaṃmataḥ yogamārgo yathānyāyaṃ śiṣyāyeha hitaiṣiṇā
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Rightly have you described, O king, the path of yoga approved by the cultivated, in due order, to a disciple, as one desiring his good.

sanskrit: sāṃkhye tv idānīṃ kārtsnyena vidhiṃ prabrūhi pṛcchate triṣu lokeṣu yaj jñānaṃ sarvaṃ tad viditaṃ hi te
english: But now, of the Sāṃkhya teaching, declare to me who ask the doctrine in its entirety; for whatever knowledge is in the three worlds, all of it is known to you.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śṛṇu me tvam idaṃ śuddhaṃ sāṃkhyānāṃ viditātmanām vihitaṃ yatibhir buddhaiḥ kapilādibhir īśvaraiḥ
english: Bhīṣma said: Hear from me this pure doctrine of the Sāṃkhyas, the knowers of the Self, ordained by enlightened ascetics, by sovereign sages such as Kapila and the rest.

sanskrit: yasmin na vibhramāḥ ke cid dṛśyante manujarṣabha guṇāś ca yasmin bahavo doṣahāniś ca kevalā
english: In which no confusions whatever are to be seen, O bull among men, in which there are many virtues and the utter removal of faults.

sanskrit: jñānena parisaṃkhyāya sadoṣān viṣayān nṛpa mānuṣān durjayān kṛtsnān paiśācān viṣayāṃs tathā
english: Having reckoned up by knowledge the faulty objects of sense, O king—the human objects, hard to conquer, in their entirety, and the objects of the piśācas likewise—

sanskrit: rākṣasān viṣayāñ jñātvā yakṣāṇāṃ viṣayāṃs tathā viṣayān auragāñ jñātvā gāndharvaviṣayāṃs tathā
english: having known the objects of the rākṣasas and likewise the objects of the yakṣas, having known the objects of the serpents and likewise the objects of the gandharvas—

sanskrit: pitṝṇāṃ viṣayāñ jñātvā tiryakṣu caratāṃ nṛpa suparṇaviṣayāñ jñātvā marutāṃ viṣayāṃs tathā
english: having known the objects of the ancestors and of creatures that move as beasts, O king, having known the objects of the suparṇas and likewise the objects of the Maruts—

sanskrit: rājarṣiviṣayāñ jñātvā brahmarṣiviṣayāṃs tathā āsurān viṣayāñ jñātvā vaiśvadevāṃs tathaiva ca
english: having known the objects of the royal sages and likewise of the brahmā sages, having known the objects of the asuras and likewise of the Viśvedevas—

sanskrit: devarṣiviṣayāñ jñātvā yogānām api ceśvarān viṣayāṃś ca prajeśānāṃ brahmaṇo viṣayāṃs tathā
english: having known the objects of the divine sages, and the lords of the yogas, and the objects of the lords of creatures, and likewise the objects of Brahmā—

sanskrit: āyuṣaś ca paraṃ kālaṃ loke vijñāya tattvataḥ sukhasya ca paraṃ tattvaṃ vijñāya vadatāṃ vara
english: and having truly understood the utmost span of life in the world, and having understood the highest truth of happiness, O best of speakers—

sanskrit: prāpte kāle ca yad duḥkhaṃ patatāṃ viṣayaiṣiṇām tiryak ca patatāṃ duḥkhaṃ patatāṃ narake ca yat
english: and the suffering that comes, when the time is at hand, to those who fall, the seekers of sense-objects—the suffering of those who fall into the state of beasts, and that of those who fall into hell—

sanskrit: svargasya ca guṇān kṛtsnān doṣān sarvāṃś ca bhārata vedavāde ca ye doṣā guṇā ye cāpi vaidikāḥ
english: and all the virtues of heaven and all its faults, O descendant of Bharata, and what faults there are in Vedic disputation, and what Vedic virtues there are—

sanskrit: jñānayoge ca ye doṣā guṇā yoge ca ye nṛpa sāṃkhyajñāne ca ye doṣās tathaiva ca guṇā nṛpa
english: and what faults there are in the yoga of knowledge and what virtues in yoga, O king, and what faults there are in the knowledge of Sāṃkhya and likewise its virtues, O king—

sanskrit: sattvaṃ daśaguṇaṃ jñātvā rajo navaguṇaṃ tathā tamaś cāṣṭaguṇaṃ jñātvā buddhiṃ saptaguṇāṃ tathā
english: having known goodness as tenfold in quality, passion as ninefold likewise, having known darkness as eightfold and the intellect as sevenfold likewise—

sanskrit: ṣaḍguṇaṃ ca nabho jñātvā manaḥ pañcaguṇaṃ tathā buddhiṃ caturguṇāṃ jñātvā tamaś ca triguṇaṃ mahat
english: having known space as sixfold and mind as fivefold likewise, having known intellect as fourfold and great darkness as threefold—

sanskrit: dviguṇaṃ ca rajo jñātvā sattvam ekaguṇaṃ punaḥ mārgaṃ vijñāya tattvena pralaye prekṣaṇaṃ tathā
english: and having known passion as twofold and goodness, again, as onefold, having understood truly the path and likewise the beholding of things at the dissolution—

sanskrit: jñānavijñānasaṃpannāḥ kāraṇair bhāvitāḥ śubhaiḥ prāpnuvanti śubhaṃ mokṣaṃ sūkṣmā iha nabhaḥ param
english: those endowed with knowledge and discernment, refined by auspicious causes, attain blessed liberation—subtle, here passing beyond into space supreme.

sanskrit: rūpeṇa dṛṣṭiṃ saṃyuktāṃ ghrāṇaṃ gandhaguṇena ca śabde saktaṃ tathā śrotraṃ jihvāṃ rasaguṇeṣu ca
english: Sight conjoined with form, and smell with the quality of odor, hearing thus attached to sound, and the tongue to the qualities of taste—

sanskrit: tanuṃ sparśe tathā saktāṃ vāyuṃ nabhasi cāśritam mohaṃ tamasi saṃsaktaṃ lobham artheṣu saṃśritam
english: the body thus attached to touch, the wind resting in space, delusion clinging to darkness, greed resting upon objects—

sanskrit: viṣṇuṃ krānte bale śakraṃ koṣṭhe saktaṃ tathānalam apsu devīṃ tathā saktām apas tejasi cāśritāḥ
english: Viṣṇu in stride, Śakra in strength, fire abiding thus in the belly, the goddess thus resting in the waters, and the waters resting upon heat—

sanskrit: tejo vāyau tu saṃsaktaṃ vāyuṃ nabhasi cāśritam nabho mahati saṃyuktaṃ mahad buddhau ca saṃśritam
english: heat clinging to the wind, the wind resting in space, space conjoined with the great principle, and the great principle resting in intellect—

sanskrit: buddhiṃ tamasi saṃsaktāṃ tamo rajasi cāśritam rajaḥ sattve tathā saktaṃ sattvaṃ saktaṃ tathātmani
english: intellect clinging to darkness, darkness resting upon passion, passion thus attached to goodness, goodness attached thus to the Self—

sanskrit: saktam ātmānam īśe ca deve nārāyaṇe tathā devaṃ mokṣe ca saṃsaktaṃ mokṣaṃ saktaṃ tu na kva cit
english: the Self attached to the Lord, and thus to the god Nārāyaṇa, the god clinging to liberation, but liberation attached to nothing whatsoever.

sanskrit: jñātvā sattvayutaṃ dehaṃ vṛtaṃ ṣoḍaśabhir guṇaiḥ svabhāvaṃ cetanāṃ caiva jñātvā vai deham āśrite
english: Having known the body joined with goodness, enveloped by the sixteen qualities, having known the inherent nature and the consciousness resident within the body—

sanskrit: madhyastham ekam ātmānaṃ pāpaṃ yasmin na vidyate dvitīyaṃ karma vijñāya nṛpate viṣayaiṣiṇām
english: having known the one Self standing in the midst, in which no evil is found, and as a second, the action of those who seek sense-objects, O king—

sanskrit: indriyāṇīndriyārthāṃś ca sarvān ātmani saṃśritān prāṇāpānau samānaṃ ca vyānodānau ca tattvataḥ
english: having truly known the senses and all the objects of the senses as resting in the Self, and the prāṇa and apāna and samāna, and the vyāna and udāna—

sanskrit: avāk caivānilaṃ jñātvā pravahaṃ cānilaṃ punaḥ sapta vātāṃs tathā śeṣān saptadhā vidhivat punaḥ
english: having known the downward-coursing wind and again the onward-bearing wind, and likewise the remaining seven winds, sevenfold, again as prescribed—

sanskrit: prajāpatīn ṛṣīṃś caiva mārgāṃś ca subahūn varān saptarṣīṃś ca bahūñ jñātvā rājarṣīṃś ca paraṃtapa
english: having known the lords of creatures and the seers, and the many excellent paths, and the many groups of seven seers, and the royal sages, O scorcher of foes—

sanskrit: surarṣīn mahataś cānyān maharṣīn sūryasaṃnibhān aiśvaryāc cyāvitāñ jñātvā kālena mahatā nṛpa
english: having known the divine seers and other great ones, the great seers resembling the sun, fallen from their sovereignty in the course of vast time, O king—

sanskrit: mahatāṃ bhūtasaṃghānāṃ śrutvā nāśaṃ ca pārthiva gatiṃ cāpy aśubhāṃ jñātvā nṛpate pāpakarmaṇām
english: having heard of the destruction of great hosts of beings, O ruler of the earth, and having known the unhappy course of those who do evil deeds, O king—

sanskrit: vaitaraṇyāṃ ca yad duḥkhaṃ patitānāṃ yamakṣaye yonīṣu ca vicitrāsu saṃsārān aśubhāṃs tathā
english: and the suffering that there is in the Vaitaraṇī for those fallen in Yama's realm, and the inauspicious transmigrations through manifold wombs—

sanskrit: jaṭhare cāśubhe vāsaṃ śoṇitodakabhājane śleṣmamūtrapurīṣe ca tīvragandhasamanvite
english: and the dwelling in the foul belly, a vessel of blood and water, amid phlegm, urine, and excrement, attended by a pungent stench—

sanskrit: śukraśoṇitasaṃghāte majjāsnāyuparigrahe sirāśatasamākīrṇe navadvāre pure 'śucau
english: in the conglomeration of seed and blood, encompassed by marrow and sinew, strewn with a hundred veins, the impure city of nine gates—

sanskrit: vijñāyāhitam ātmānaṃ yogāṃś ca vividhān nṛpa tāmasānāṃ ca jantūnāṃ ramaṇīyāvṛtātmanām
english: having understood the Self thus lodged, and the various yogas, O king, and of creatures sunk in darkness, their selves enveloped by what seems pleasant—

sanskrit: sāttvikānāṃ ca jantūnāṃ kutsitaṃ bharatarṣabha garhitaṃ mahatām arthe sāṃkhyānāṃ viditātmanām
english: and of creatures of the quality of goodness—what is despicable, O bull of the Bhāratas, and what is censured in the estimation of the great, the Sāṃkhyas who know the Self—

sanskrit: upaplavāṃs tathā ghorāñ śaśinas tejasas tathā tārāṇāṃ patanaṃ dṛṣṭvā nakṣatrāṇāṃ ca paryayam
english: having beheld the dread eclipses of the moon and likewise of the sun, the falling of the stars, and the wheeling round of the constellations—

sanskrit: dvaṃdvānāṃ viprayogaṃ ca vijñāya kṛpaṇaṃ nṛpa anyonyabhakṣaṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūtānām api cāśubham
english: and having understood the pitiful sundering of paired ones, O king, and having beheld the inauspicious devouring of one another among living beings—

sanskrit: bālye mohaṃ ca vijñāya kṣayaṃ dehasya cāśubham rāge mohe ca saṃprāpte kva cit sattvaṃ samāśritam
english: and having understood the delusion of childhood and the inauspicious decay of the body, and goodness somewhere taking refuge when passion and delusion have come upon one—

sanskrit: sahasreṣu naraḥ kaś cin mokṣabuddhiṃ samāśritaḥ durlabhatvaṃ ca mokṣasya vijñāya śrutipūrvakam
english: among thousands some one man takes refuge in the resolve for liberation; and having understood, on the authority of scripture, the difficulty of attaining liberation—

sanskrit: bahumānam alabdheṣu labdhe madhyasthatāṃ punaḥ viṣayāṇāṃ ca daurātmyaṃ vijñāya nṛpate punaḥ
english: the high regard for things unattained, and again indifference once they are attained, and having understood, again, the wickedness of the objects of sense, O king—

sanskrit: gatāsūnāṃ ca kaunteya dehān dṛṣṭvā tathāśubhān vāsaṃ kuleṣu jantūnāṃ duḥkhaṃ vijñāya bhārata
english: and having beheld the inauspicious bodies of those whose breath has gone, O son of Kuntī, and having understood the suffering of dwelling among the families of creatures, O descendant of Bharata—

sanskrit: brahmaghnānāṃ gatiṃ jñātvā patitānāṃ sudāruṇām surāpāne ca saktānāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ durātmanām gurudāraprasaktānāṃ gatiṃ vijñāya cāśubhām
english: having known the dreadful destiny of the slayers of brāhmaṇas, the fallen, and of evil-souled brāhmaṇas addicted to the drinking of liquor, and having known the inauspicious destiny of those given over to the wives of their teachers—
